q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026 (6 days from today, August 20, 2026). The forward guidance will be announced at that time.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA will provide forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 revenue in the range of approximately **100-105 billion dollars**.

**Reasoning:**
- **Recent guidance pattern**: NVIDIA guided Q2 FY2027 at $91.0B ±2% (issued May 20, 2026)
- **Actual performance**: Q1 FY2027 came in at $81.6B, beating guidance by ~$2B
- **Q2 consensus**: Wall Street estimates range from $91.9B to $93.5B, suggesting NVIDIA will likely beat or meet its $91B guidance
- **Sequential growth trajectory**: Q1 $81.6B → Q2 ~$91-93B suggests ~12% QoQ growth
- **Forward momentum**: If Q2 comes in at the upper end of analyst expectations (~$93-94B), Q3 guidance would likely reflect continued strong demand with modest sequential growth
- **Typical guidance philosophy**: NVIDIA tends to provide conservative guidance that it can beat. If Q2 materially exceeds guidance, Q3 guidance would likely be in the $100-105B range, representing ~8-12% sequential growth

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Demand weakness signals**: Macro uncertainty, customer inventory corrections, or weaker-than-expected data center spending would compress guidance
- **China restrictions tightening**: Further export controls on Chinese data center revenue could dampen growth
- **Competitive pressures**: If AMD or other competitors gain meaningful share, NVIDIA might guide more conservatively
- **Guidance miss in Q2**: If Q2 actual revenue disappoints relative to consensus, Q3 guidance would be lower
- **Conservative posture**: NVIDIA might be more cautious given macro uncertainties

Target: **95-105 billion** (lower distribution tail)

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Strong Q2 beat**: If Q2 revenue exceeds $94-95B (above current consensus), confidence in Q3 would be higher
- **Accelerating demand**: Continued robust AI/data center spending, new customer wins, or fuller ramp of newer products
- **China developments**: Any easing of export restrictions could unlock additional revenue potential
- **Installed base momentum**: Larger customer bases deploying more GPUs faster than expected
- **Inventory normalization**: If previously suppressed demand releases, could drive stronger growth
- **Product cycle**: New products ramping faster or at higher ASPs than expected

Target: **105-115+ billion** (upper distribution tail)

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 actual: **$81.6 billion**
- Q2 FY2027 guidance issued: **$91.0 billion ±2%** (range: $89.2-$92.8B)
- Q2 Wall Street consensus: **$91.9-$93.5 billion**
- Q1 beat guidance by approximately $2 billion

NVIDIA's recent pattern shows:
1. Conservative guidance (Q1 beat by ~$2B on $89B guidance)
2. Sequential growth of roughly 10-12% per quarter in current environment
3. Wall Street consistently estimating slightly above guidance but below realized performance

## Analysis of the provided range (99.5-115.5B)

The range suggests the forecaster expects **Q3 FY2027 forward guidance** to land in this zone. This makes sense:
- **Lower bound (99.5B)**: Represents ~7-9% sequential growth from Q2 (conservative scenario)
- **Upper bound (115.5B)**: Represents ~25% sequential growth from Q2 (aggressive scenario)
- **Midpoint (~107B)**: Represents ~15-17% sequential growth from Q2 (moderate scenario)

Given NVIDIA's recent beat pattern, strong AI momentum, and that the range is positioned well above current guidance, I expect guidance to land toward the middle-to-upper portion of this range.

## Probability distribution reasoning

- **Below 99.5B** (5-10%): Would require weaker-than-expected Q2 results or significant demand deterioration
- **99.5-105B** (40%): Conservative growth continuing ~10-12% sequentially, typical NVIDIA pattern
- **105-110B** (35%): Strong Q2 beat with confidence in sustained momentum
- **110-115.5B** (15%): Very strong Q2 beat and significant upside surprise from current expectations
- **Above 115.5B** (5%): Would require exceptional beat and very strong forward demand signals

My median estimate centers around **107 billion**, reflecting:
- High confidence Q2 will beat the $91B guidance (likely $93-94B actual)
- NVIDIA's pattern of conservative guidance allowing for beats
- Continued strong AI demand momentum
- Typical sequential growth rate of ~15% (conservative to moderate pace)

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 revenue is not yet available. The company is scheduled to report its Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026, after the market closes, at which point it will provide its outlook for the next quarter [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026).

For the current Q2 FY2027, which ended approximately late July 2026, NVIDIA's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, is for revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly assumes no data center compute revenue from China [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts, on average, are estimating Q2 FY2027 revenue closer to $91.9 billion, with some aggregators pegging it nearer $93.5 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026/). In Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported revenue of $81.6 billion, exceeding its guidance by approximately $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
